steps.text: You're leaving today?
The Godmother only just gave you that staff, and all the things in the castle are still unsorted. Is it really so urgent?
It'll soon be time. No matter what, I cannot deliver things late.
Don't forget. We abide by agreements, and we never break promises.
I wasn't saying that. I just think it's all too sudden.
You could've chosen something much simpler first. Like choosing a well-behaved child to welcome at the castle, or giving the boys and girls sweet dreams. That sort.
It'd all be better than trying to find a girl from over ten years ago. We only know the name, and you lack any experience, Iris...
I do indeed lack experience.
But out of everyone who preceded me, none ever gave up a promise for its difficulty.
Sigh... Fine. If you insist, I can't stop you.
Then this metal thing. Yes. Keep it well.
Is this—a radio?
An obsolete kind. I fancy it'll barely receive the closest waves nowadays.
Keep jabbing at it like that, and you might jab it apart.
Here, for you. It'll be useful on the way, and I've kept the details packed with.
Oh, thank you.
I'm not that careless!
I've kept it nice! Letting someone else have it does not reassure me! You'd better not break it on the way!
You're worrying too much. That'd never happen!
Easy enough to say.
What...!
Now, now, enough fuss. No-one doubts your capability. We're all very aware.
It's only normal that everyone should worry for you on your first outing.
Hm-hmph.

You must stay safe outside, and safer still in front of strangers. Your transport is all ready. Remember to keep its parts maintained along your journey. Before you enter the wilderness, you must take full caution...
Ah, I've gone on too long. Regardless of anything, prioritize protecting yourself.
I know... I understand. Don't worry. It may be quite trying, but it'll be fine.
I must see this agreement through to the end. It's already been far too long since we set foot outdoors.
The children believe in us, and that's why they give us their cherished belongings for our safekeeping. We must return them as arranged. We cannot let their trust be in vain.
And so, even if they've grown up, and they no longer believe, I'll prove it to them still.
I'll prove—
that fairytales are everlasting.
I see. Then may all go well for you.
We look forward to your return. Iris.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Oh, I'm finally here.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (By the records, back then, the child should've been around here when she was taken in.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Tonnerre Village. The child's name was... Mabel. Good, all in order.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (But is... is this a village?)

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Hey, careful, little miss.

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Don't go any further in, you'll mess up your shoes. Shoes like those, it'd be a shame if you did! We'd never afford to pay!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Thank you for the warning.

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: No problem.

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: You seem like a little miss from a good old family. No escort with you? What're you up to in this kind of place?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I don't need an escort. I'm just looking for someone.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Moreover, this is Victoria. What's the problem with Victorian people being on their own soil?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Ha! Well put! Well put, little miss. Of course it's safest for our own people in our own home!

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: But still, best you watch out. You're young yet. See, there's been disturbance in the city recently. Careful where you step.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: The city...?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Er, never mind. What goes on in the city is nothing to do with me.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I've given you an answer. I think it's fair you give me one now.

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: What's your question?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I came here to find someone, but...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Shouldn't there be a village here? Why don't I see anyone else?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: A village?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: See for yourself, little miss. What looks like a village here to you?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: There used to be a few villages around here, mind, but they've all left now. Old noble boy snapped this place up. There'll be construction starting this spring. Building a factory!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: ...A factory...

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Look here, this metal sheet, and this giant thing! Majestic, isn't it? Goes vrrmm!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: It's—it's very cool.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: But, the factory... Why here? Why not on a nomadic plate?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: The old noble boy builds wherever he pleases. It's ours to ask why.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Could you tell me where all those villages here migrated to?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: What? Who the hell knows...

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Can't have moved far, I'll tell you that. This area's solid, after all, close to the city orbits. You only see refugees with nowhere to go head for the wastes!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I understand. Thank you very much.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (...Still within expectations.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (It's already been close to twenty years. It wouldn't be odd for the child's village to relocate between then and now...)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (I'll only be able to search a little bit of the surrounding area. At least the village's name, and the name of the child are still recorded. If worse comes to worst, I'll enter the city and see what I can do to find them.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Hmph. A hurdle this trifling could never stop me!)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Excuse me, is this Tonnerre Village?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: It's not? Alright, thank you, sorry to bother you.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Hello, could I ask if anyone knows a girl named Mabel... erm, sorry, she should be a lady of about twenty. Does anyone know her?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I see, then...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Thank you, I'll go somewhere else and see if I can ask.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Sorry for the bother, but is this Tonnerre Village...?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Excuse me...
Iris recalled the words she grew up with—To protect a paradise, a fragile dream, is never an easy thing.
It was only to fulfill a promise, to allow slumberland to last forever in the children's fledgling hearts. They always gave it their utmost, their all.
Dazzling dreamlands far-flung from reality became the gentle croons of nursery rhymes, broken into phrases kept in stories handed down across the land, down across hundreds and thousands of years.
She didn't want to give up.
She couldn't give up.
In fairytales, nothing was ever unachievable.
Within reality, achievement could only ask one's dedication to the task.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Southwards from this road, and then turn east... pass through the forests here...)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (There's a roadsign here. Mm. I should be going the right way.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (How many villages is this now? This is already the nomadic city's periphery plate. Look any further in, and I'll be entering the city...)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Or perhaps, I should head outwards...)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Never mind. I'd better find somewhere to keep the vehicle safe first.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Hm? What's that sound?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Daddy, are we going home?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Is my disease all better now? It still hurts... aren't we going to the doctor?

steps.name: Man
steps.text: We're going home... we're not going to the hospital, we're going home.

steps.name: Man
steps.text: Daddy bought you medicine. We'll go home and take it, and then it won't hurt, Dora.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Huh? Do I have to take really bitter medicine again...? I don't wanna take it! No!

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: Dora, listen carefully, if you take your medicine your illness will be better.  So even if it's bitter, you have to be brave, okay?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: But it's so bitter...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Last time, that burnt up paper was really hard to swallow. And then before that, the injecshun really hurt... mummy, can I stop seeing the doctor? I don't wanna get injecshuns, and I don't wanna take more medicine.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Can I go outside and play? I miss my friends at school. Maemae came to ask when I can play with her the day before. I wanna go out and play with her...

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: (Sob)

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Mummy, are you crying...?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Don't cry, mummy! I... I'll take my medicine, and I won't go outside at all! I'll stop complaining!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I'll listen to mummy and daddy. I'll be a good girl. So stop crying, mummy...

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: Dora, Dora... you're a good girl... why did it have to be you, why did it have to be you!?

steps.name: Man
steps.text: My poor girl... oh...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (An ill child...)

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: This mission's about over now. Give it the stamp for me.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: By the way, I brought some fruit from the south for Maemae. Are these the ones she threw a fit about wanting last time?

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: You even brought something? You really are too kind.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Thank you for these, they're just the ones. Don't spoil her too much, now. Her teeth will fall out if she keeps eating sweet things all day!

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: The only thing on her mind all day is play. Oh, this morning she insisted to me a fairy took her to stay at a castle last night. I think I've been telling her too many bedtime stories. She's still so silly, even at her age.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: She's still little.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: She's not little, she's almost about to go to school. Let's see... no issues with the mission. Do I just stamp on here for you?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: That'll do.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Certainly. Have this back.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: You came back fairly fast this time. What's the city like now?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Much better than I was expecting. Some talking politics in coffee shops, but just talking. Gatherings are peaceful.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Aside from the culture nuts, normal folk like us don't care about the political stuff, after all.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: There were some workers making a commotion on the street the day before because their payslips were too low, but nobody got hurt, thankfully.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Sounds like it wasn't much of an incident.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Who's that girl? She's not a local, is she?

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Who? Oh, you mean her... you've got sharp eyes. Out of the blue, she came to this village just about yesterday.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: It sounds like she's looking for someone. First she asked the village's name, and that seemed right, and then she started going from house to house, asking.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: All she has is a name. Can't be easy finding them.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: I don't know how far she's been already, but that craft she came in's been dinged and scraped up to Hell and back. It's parked up by Mr. Eason's right now, waiting for repairs.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: The girl doesn't give up, I'll tell you that.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: We all want to help her too. Maemae's been helping her since the crack of dawn, running all over to knock and ask, and plenty of the kids with, all raring to go.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: She's coming over.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Excuse me.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Can I ask if Maemae's back yet?

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Not yet. Don't know where she's run off to.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: How's it been going for you? Still haven't found who you're looking for?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Not yet, no.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What kind of person are you looking for?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What kind of person are you?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: You look out of place. And all goggled and masked, how suspicious!

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Hahahahaha!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Hey.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Ha, haha... she's not wrong, you know. First time I saw you, I was thinking the same thing!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Do I really look that shifty?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: The last thing I tell is lies!

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Here, Miss, don't wrinkle your brow like that. Tell him about who you're looking for. Ignore him dressing like he's dangerous. He's actually a quite reliable guy.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Really? Er...

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Don't your eyes hurt, glaring at each other so hard?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: It's fine. I'm used to it.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Never mind. I'm not arguing with you.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: And I'm not arguing with a child.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Scowl)

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Keep some things to yourself!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Seeing as you already know I'm looking for someone, why not tell you, I suppose.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Mabel. I'm looking for Mabel Grimm.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I don't like repeating myself.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Oh, don't you start glaring at each other again.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I'm not that puerile!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I... in all honesty, I've never met her. But I know she's called Mabel, she's a Feline, and she has brown hair and green eyes.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: She should be roughly under thirty, and she's very nimble with her hands... That's all I've heard.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: But... I've gone around every single house in the village, and I still haven't found a clue whatsoever.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Is this really Tonnerre Village? I'd hate it if all along I'd gotten the name wrong...

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: As sad it is to say, Miss, there's all too many villages whose names sound like ours. And your records aren't all that specific, not to mention, you're looking for someone from all those years ago.

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Oh, don't, now. Don't feel down. I'm sure you'll find her!

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: I remember there were a few more houses in the forest beside the village. Have you been over there, yet?

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: Worst comes to worst... to worst, mind you, give this fella a shout. Get him to take this mission on, and help you out!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Oi. Wait a moment. Rhodes Island's missions all need to be registered, first...

steps.name: Ordinary Clerk
steps.text: (Whisper) Stop it with the office talk. The mission you had is done, isn't it! Look, are you going to help her, or not?!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (Whisper) ...Fine.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What are you plotting, all mysterious over there...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What are you doing, following me?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Helping you.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I don't need it!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (Shrug)

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: You'll leave the village out this way. Going to visit the houses out on the edge?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Mm. I can do it on my own. This is my job. I don't need you to help!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Child labor?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: *cough*. Nothing.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Actually, I wanted to say, about the person you're looking for. I probably know them...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: —Shh!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Wait, stop for a moment!)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Did you hear... a voice just now?)

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: No! I won't have it!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Are you afraid?! You're afraid, aren't you?! You're scared of being sentenced, so you'd give our daughter over?!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: I won't let you do anything of the sort!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: You can't give them Dora, they'll take her away, throw her into isolation! She's got a whole life ahead of her, and if she goes in there, she'll never come out again!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: This is my child, this is our bloody child! How could you?!

steps.name: Man's Voice
steps.text: Just calm down—keep it down a little!

steps.name: Man's Voice
steps.text: Why in the hell would I give Dora to them? I never said that! It's just—it's just, how can you bear to see her like this?

steps.name: Man's Voice
steps.text: We can't cure her... we've tried every drug, we've taken her for every treatment they told us... Useless, all of it's been useless!

steps.name: Man's Voice
steps.text: There's already people suspicious of us because we're going and buying medicine! We can't keep hiding this! We need to figure out something soon!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: We'll—We'll leave this place. We'll take Dora, and we won't stay here anymore. We can go somewhere where nobody lives—

steps.name: Man's Voice
steps.text: And where do we have to go?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (The voices are coming from this side. Hrm... here. This house.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (They were talking about...)

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (Their daughter catching Oripathy, most likely.)

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: (Hiding Infected. In Victoria, that's a fairly grave offence.)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: (Dora... I've heard the name before...)

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I'm going to take a look!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: —Hold on, oi!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: She acts on the first word she hears... honestly, what a child.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: What's the time, Mr. Wolf? ...3 o'clock!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: What's the time, Mr. Wolf? ...Dinnertime!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: This is no fun.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Dolly, dolly, I wish you could move. Then you could play with me.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Dolly, when do you think mummy and daddy will finally let me go outside?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I don't want to be ill. I hate being ill.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: My arm hurts... my belly hurts too...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Don't scratch. If you scratch, it might get even worse.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: (Covers mouth)

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: (Whisper) Who... who are you!?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: (Whisper) How did you come in? The windows are all closed... um, wait, you should get out quick! If my mummy and daddy find you, they'll get mad at us!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Windows like that can't stop me. It's okay, nobody will find us.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Were you playing something just now?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Do you want this doll to move, and play with you?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Of course! But... how does a dolly move?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: There's ways. Aren't there all sorts of little creatures in storybooks who can speak? If there are puppets who can be people, and cats who can walk on two legs, then of course there are dollies who can move.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Hm... do you like listening to stories?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I do! Mummy's told me lots of stories before!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Like the child in the chimney, and the one with big scissors, and the garden with a fairy...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: And the one about a castle with tea parties!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: It's really, really big, and really, really pretty, and only good children can go to it, and inside, there's these really nice fairies, and they give you really nice cakes and stuff, and they have a tea party all day...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: And you can grab the clouds out of the sky, and they taste really sweet, too...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I really want to go to the castle, and be in the tea party, so, I've been trying really hard all the time to be a good girl. When will the fairies pick me up to go to the castle?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Perhaps, very soon, you'll have the chance.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: You're a good girl. I'm sure you will!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Really? That's super!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: When I go to the castle, will my dolly start moving, and play with me?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Mm-hm. You've heard it in stories, haven't you? At the fairies' castle, if you're a good child, they'll keep your most beloved treasures safe, and when the time comes, those treasures will come back to your side once again.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Dollies who live in the castle aren't ordinary dollies. They can move, and sing, and play games with you!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Do you want your dolly to come 'alive?'

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I... I really do...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: But, do I have to leave my dolly behind?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: If I have to, then I don't want to...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Wh... why?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: It won't take too much time. My friends... I mean, the fairies are really powerful, and I'm sure they'll let your dolly move in no time!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Just make sure everything's agreed, and your dolly will be back by your side before you know it!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: My mummy and daddy gave me this dolly for my birthday. I don't want to leave her.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: When I got my dolly, I told mummy that I'd protect her forever! I have to protect my own little girl, right?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Why do people all leave their treasure and stuff so the fairies can keep 'em?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: But you're—

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: ...But you're...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: You're fallen ill...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: If one day someone else finds you, they could take you away. If they really do, then you'll have no way to protect your dolly, right...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Um... daddy said the same thing, too.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: But, it's okay. I'll stay at home like they told me. Mummy and daddy won't let me get taken away!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: My dolly is my little girl, and I'll protect my dolly. Mummy and daddy said I'm their little girl, and mummy and daddy will protect me.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: So as long as I listen to them and be a good girl, I won't get taken away!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I can accept that...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Hehee. Thank you for worrying about me.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Oh, um, I still haven't asked your name yet. Are you sure mummy and daddy won't find us? You're not... from our village, right? I've never seen you before.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I'm Dora. What about you?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I'm... Iris.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Iris!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Can you... can you play with me for a bit? Just a tiny bit!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: It's too boring by myself, and I can't play outside, so I can only draw stuff at home, and play jigsaws... and I've played them forever and I'm bored...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: You can't go outside?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: If I say I wanna go outside, then mummy will cry. 'Cause I've got a really bad disease, and if I go outside when I want, then bad people will take me away.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: They'll take me away, and then I'll never see mummy and daddy again.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I don't wanna make mummy cry, and I don't want to leave mummy and daddy behind. But...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: But I miss Maemae and all my friends, and I wanna go back to school.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Oh, don't feel down... I'll—I'll play with you!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Do you like this one? Or this toy here, see, if you press it, it lights up! Let's play jigsaws for now, and then next time I'll bring you a new ragdoll—

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I'm sorry, this is as much as I can do... I don't have any way to let you go outside.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Iris, why are you being all weird and apolojettic? You didn't do anything wrong.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Um, do you think, if I really see a Miss Fairy, I can make a wish to her?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Of course you can! Fairies are enormously powerful!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: That's great! Will the Miss Fairies in the castle cure my disease?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: The Miss Fairies can't do everything, either...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I see, then...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: B—But!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Even if they don't have a way to cure your disease! If you have any other desires as well, I'm sure they can—

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Then, I want mummy to never cry again. Can they do that?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: That's—That's not possible, but if you have anything else!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Um... I want to grow up a little faster, too.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: That can't be done, either.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: It can't...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: None of it can be done...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Then never mind.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Dora, aren't you disappointed?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Don't you feel like... the fairies are so useless, that the fairytales are all liars?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I'm gonna tell you a secret. You can't tell anyone else! Actually, my best friend Maemae came to play with me this morning, but she couldn't come in, so we talked through the window all secret.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Maemae said, last night, a Miss Fairy invited her to the castle, and Maemae wouldn't lie to me! She said it was like a dream in there, and the cakes and biscuits were all super tasty!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Maemae's a good girl too...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Mm-hm! But, if I meet a Miss Fairy, I won't mention any of the wishes from just now. Iris, you have to keep it a secret, too!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: A secret? Why?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Um, because, think about it! If the Miss Fairy knew she couldn't make my wishes come true, then she'd feel really bad. So I can't tell her about them.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: You've finally come out. Are you done talking with that girl in there?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: How did you know?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Had a chat with her mother and father, and I heard movement from the rooms inside.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What's wrong? Didn't go well?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: It's none of your business...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: How are her parents? Are they truly thinking about handing their daughter over?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: I can reassure you, they don't want their daughter to leave their side. They just... can't think of another way.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: And on the off-chance someone else finds them, what'll happen?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Hrm... I'm guessing they'd immediately take the poorly girl away, and throw her in an isolation ward. The parents are harboring hidden Infected, so in all likelihood, they'd be sentenced too.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: But you don't need to worry about that too much right now. I've already introduced them to somewhere reliable.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What kind of place could even be reliable for people stuck in their situation?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I know what Dora has is Oripathy, and I know it's an awful disease with no current cure...

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: What kind of place is it, huh... hrmm, it's a little hard to describe.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: But it's essentially somewhere where their daughter can receive treatment. Not somewhere where people just get split apart and left to die, or directly hung, or condemned to work in factories.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: ...It sounds like it has something going for it.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Obviously. But it's just a possibility I gave to them. It's up to them how they decide.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Victorian people have a strange sense of pride and superiority about their country and its soil. I've had the pleasure of knowing that more times than I can count.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What in the world makes you... are you being sarcastic?!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Ah... I don't mean it that way.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: It's just that—throwing away your current life in pursuit of a single possibility, that's something much easier said than done. Even if they opted to go on as things are in the end, I wouldn't be surprised any.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: That girl fallen ill still believes in fairytales. She's still that young.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: I can't help her... she's a good child, but I—don't have anything I can do for her. One story, one dreamland. None of it, nearly enough to rescue her from her ailment...

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: But they let people have hope.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: I might not know what's gnawing at you right now, but I think stories and sweet dreams are good things.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Wonderful things let people yearn, and let them have hope. In awful circumstances like these, letting people hold onto their longing for wonderful things like that, I think, is essential.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: After all, we need to first know what's good, and that's how we can have a direction to strive in, am I right?

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Then tell me about you. Do you believe in fairytales?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: I believe in some things even more idealistic than fairytales. If those count as fairytales too, then yes, I believe.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Don't let it weigh on you. There's so little we can do for others in the first place.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Right, you said you were looking for someone before...

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: If you have no other trails, then I actually know a girl called Mabel.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: I know she was originally Victorian, she's twenty-odd, brown-haired, green-eyed, and very nimble with her hands, though she's not a lover of manual work. She just likes fiddling with machine parts.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: For the moment... she matches up completely with your account.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: —! She matches so thoroughly; this can't just be a coincidence!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Where is she?! Tell me where she is!

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Mm-hm. I've actually gotten more sure the more I think about it.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: But, if she's really the one you're looking for, then you're actually a little late now.

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Certain things happening that probably aren't be up to me to tell.

steps.name: Field Operator
steps.text: Or... maybe you should try going to meet her.
